note: Ratchet for scripts/check-entry-budget.mjs. entryJsGzBytes pins the current entry weight and may only go DOWN; targetGzBytes is the 350 KiB v1.0 budget from RELEASE-GATE.md.

loweredOn.by: lazy-loading the self-host first-run wizard off the /setup route
loweredOn.measured: 309,727 bytes (302.5 KiB gz), down from 313,583 measured on the same inputs — 3.8 KiB gz out of the entry, 47.5 KiB under the 350 KiB v1.0 target.
loweredOn.why: The connection-pause wave added ~0.2 KiB gz of genuinely entry-resident weight (18 en-US strings in the eagerly-bundled `common` catalogue, and the 13th system state) and the gate went red by 183 bytes — the 1,956-byte margin left on 2026-08-24 had already been spent by ordinary additions since. Attributing the entry source map (the 2026-08-18 lesson: attribute, never infer from the changelog) found `app/router.tsx` importing `SetupPage` statically, which put `FirstRunWizard` and `TelemetryConsent` (3,869 + 3,171 raw attributed bytes) in the synchronous set for every user on every route. That wizard runs ONCE per instance, before anybody has an account, and its own route guard redirects to /login the moment a super admin exists — so on a configured install it is the one screen a returning user provably cannot reach, and everybody was downloading it anyway. Its desktop twin `/desktop/setup` was already lazy; this is the same click.
loweredOn.headroom: 2,000 bytes — the usual minifier-drift margin, not growth room.
loweredOn.cost: One chunk fetch on the single visit to /setup a given instance ever makes — behind the same Suspense-null fallback the other deferred routes use, and overlapping the `setupStateQuery()` round trip the route guard already awaits before the component renders.
loweredOn.notAnException: The static set is deliberately the FIRST PAINT — auth screens, AppShell, HomePage, PageRenderer, the system states, the 404 (see the note above `lazyRoute` in app/router.tsx). /setup is not first paint for a returning user; it is unreachable for one.

previousLoweredOn.by: lazy-loading ScheduledReportsPage out of the reports route factory (30-record-pages.md D8)
previousLoweredOn.measured: 311,444 bytes (304.1 KiB gz), down from 317,993 measured on the same inputs — 6.4 KiB gz out of the entry, 45.9 KiB under the 350 KiB v1.0 target.
previousLoweredOn.why: The record-pages wave added ~0.4 KiB gz of genuinely entry-resident code (TemplateMount's detail-template resolution, the table→slug resolver, the record-open routing) and the gate went red — the 2,016-byte margin left on 2026-08-20 had already been spent by ordinary additions since. Attributing the entry source map (the 2026-08-18 lesson: attribute, never infer from the changelog) found `reports/routes.tsx` importing `ScheduledReportsPage` statically, which put the manager AND the `ScheduledJobsList` calendar family from @adminium/widgets in the synchronous set for every user on every route — the exact shape the 2026-08-18/20 lazifications removed everywhere else. The route body now loads on first open of /reports, behind the same Suspense-null fallback the other admin screens use.
previousLoweredOn.headroom: 1,956 bytes — the usual minifier-drift margin, not growth room.
previousLoweredOn.cost: One chunk fetch the first time /reports is opened.

previouslyLoweredOn.by: deferring the two data-io route bodies, which is what finally made the page-wizard template split real
previouslyLoweredOn.measured: 315,684 bytes (308.3 KiB gz), down from 330,905 on the same build inputs — 14.9 KiB gz out of the entry, and 42.7 KiB under the 350 KiB v1.0 target.
previouslyLoweredOn.why: `app/router.tsx` imports `data-io/routes.tsx` statically — it has to, the routes are built at module scope — and that module imported `ImportWizardPage` and `DataExportsPage` statically, so both route bodies were in the synchronously-loaded set for every user on every route. `ImportWizardPage` is ALSO the `page-wizard` template body, so the lazy binding `pages/templates.tsx` registers for `page-wizard` was a NO-OP: its chunk held a 22-line wrapper while the body shipped on boot regardless. Thirteen of the fourteen template bindings were genuinely deferred and the accounting said fourteen. Both are deferred now, so both are what they claim to be.

whatMoved.ImportWizardPage: the bulk of it: the wizard pulls @adminium/widgets' PageWizard, UploadDropzone, ColumnMappingTableWidget and ValidationIssuesListWidget along with their zod config schemas.
whatMoved.DataExportsPage: the exports manager, a route body with no second life as a template.

previouslyLoweredOn.headroom: 2,016 bytes — the same margin the click below left, and for the same reason: enough to absorb minifier drift, not enough to hide growth.
previouslyLoweredOn.cost: One chunk fetch the first time /imports or /exports is opened. The page surface and its topbar title stay outside the Suspense boundary, so the frame paints on the first frame and only the body waits behind a centered spinner.
previouslyLoweredOn.whatThisNumberIsNot: The gate builds its asset list from two regexes that both hardcode `\.js`, so the entry STYLESHEET is uncounted: `index.css` is a plain <link> in <head> with no media trick and blocks paint. Measured on this build it is 20,955 bytes gz, which puts the real blocking payload at 336,639 against the 358,400 target — 21,761 bytes of room, not 42,716. Widening the gate to count CSS (and the self-hosted woff2 faces, also uncounted) is a separate change; recording the number here is so the JS figure is not read as the whole story.
previouslyLoweredOn.drift: The 331,000 this came down from was already loose: a fresh build measured 330,905 before this change, against the 329,014 the record below pinned. Nothing raised the ratchet — ordinary additions spent the margin (60 locale keys and two now-static icons on 2026-08-19, then 20 SMTP + export strings on 2026-08-20, ~1.4 KiB gz between them), which is exactly the drift a ratchet is meant to make visible and a stale one hides. RELEASE-GATE.md now states this measurement in both places it records the entry chunk.

priorLoweredOn.by: lazy-loading the page templates and the non-first-paint routes, and removing the lucide barrel
priorLoweredOn.measured: 329,014 bytes (321.3 KiB gz), down from 670,786 — a 51% reduction. **Under the 350 KiB v1.0 target for the first time.**
priorLoweredOn.why: The four raises of 2026-08-17 and the note below them all attributed this gate's growth to the en-US i18n catalogue and named 10-T06's namespace split as the fix — 'the single highest-leverage item', 'it would return all three of today's raises and then some'. That was measured for the first time on 2026-08-18 and it is wrong. Deleting EN_US_RESOURCES entirely and rebuilding gives 48.7 KiB gz: real, a seventh of what was actually available, and nowhere near a 305 KiB gap. Attributing the entry chunk's own source map instead found the weight in three places nobody had looked at.

whatItActuallyWas.1. page templates, -97.0 KiB gz: `pages/templates.tsx` statically imported all fourteen page-template bindings, and each pulls a template component out of @adminium/widgets. A page renders exactly ONE template, so thirteen were downloaded by every user on every route and never executed. `resolvePageTemplate` was already async and `TemplateMount` already rendered a skeleton for its resolving phase — the machinery was built and then fed a synchronous map.
whatItActuallyWas.2. the lucide barrel, -112.6 KiB gz: `packages/ui`'s `Icon` and the dashboard's `lucideByName` both resolved an icon from a runtime name via `import { icons } from 'lucide-react'`. A map lookup is opaque to a bundler, so all 1,611 icon modules were emitted — verified in the source map, all 1,611 with non-zero attributed bytes — for the ~136 the product draws. `scripts/gen-icon-core.mjs` now emits those as named imports; the full catalogue is a dynamic import that only a hand-picked icon outside the set pulls in.
whatItActuallyWas.3. route components, -62.7 KiB gz: Eleven route components were statically imported in `app/router.tsx`, so they were in the synchronously-loaded set on every route. `EmailTemplatesPage` was the expensive one by an order of magnitude: it shares the block canvas with `page-builder`, so importing it reached `PageBuilder` → `WidgetHost` → the whole widget REGISTRY, 23 families of definitions and Zod config schemas, 336 KiB minified. The rest — About, API keys, Changelog, KB, Account, Preferences, Notifications, Defaults, Desktop settings, Desktop setup, Onboarding — are ordinary admin screens.

priorLoweredOn.whatWasDeliberatelyNotDone: Removing the en-US catalogue from the entry, i.e. the thing the previous entries recommended. It is worth 48.7 KiB gz and the target no longer needs it, but it is not free: `t(key, fallback)` passes the fallback as i18next's `defaultValue`, so en-US would render from the CALL SITES instead of the catalogue — and comparing all 2,052 single-quoted call sites against `common.json` found five that have drifted. Two of them are the catalogue carrying an ICU plural (`{count, plural, one {# column} other {# columns}}`) where the fallback is a bare `{count} columns`, so the swap would ship '1 columns'. The catalogue is authoritative in those places and the fallbacks are stale; reconciling them is real work, and it is not a bundle-size task.
priorLoweredOn.headroom: 1,986 bytes (~1.9 KiB). Wider than the ~400 the raise entries left, because the ratchet is no longer the binding constraint — the v1.0 target is 27 KiB below it and that is what should be defended now.
priorLoweredOn.cost: One chunk fetch the first time a page of a given template is opened, and one the first time an admin screen is opened — both behind the <Suspense> fallbacks those routes already rendered. The first paint (auth screens, AppShell, HomePage, PageRenderer, the system states, the 404) is untouched and stays static by design.

supersededHistory.note: Six raise/lower entries from 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-17 lived here in full. They are dropped rather than kept, because four of them recorded the same wrong diagnosis in increasing detail and leaving them would preserve the reasoning that produced four raises in one day. The record that matters is above: what was believed, what was measured, and the difference.
supersededHistory.theLesson: Every one of those entries reasoned about the cause from what had just been added — 'this feature added 110 strings, the entry grew, therefore strings' — and none attributed the chunk it was measuring. The entry's own source map answers the question directly in about a minute, and it named three causes none of which were the one four consecutive entries agreed on.
